meta.title: BCSentinel – Estimated Loss explained transparently
meta.description: Transparent Estimated Loss examples for data-quality issues in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.

hero.title: Understand how a data issue becomes a defensible business impact.
hero.lead: BCSentinel separates directly measured scan values from documented model assumptions. This makes clear what comes from Business Central, how the calculation works, and why a finding matters to the business.

summary.title: A number is useful only when its origin remains understandable.
summary.lead: Estimated Loss is not an accounted financial loss. It is a modeled decision-support value that makes recurring rework, delays, control effort, and other operational friction visible.

method.title: Five factors make the model calculation understandable.
method.lead: Not every finding necessarily uses the same weighting. The general principle remains consistent: detected scope is combined with conservative process assumptions.
factors: Scope measured directly by the scan.
How often the condition creates actual process effort.
Conservative manual effort per relevant case.
Blended internal hourly rate for the business case.
How often the effect occurs during the period.

examples.title: Five complete examples from different business areas.
examples.lead: Each example shows business relevance, measured scope, assumptions, formula, result, and a concrete recommended action.

items.title: Sales lines with price 0
items.why: Zero-price sales lines often create invoice corrections, coordination effort, and margin leakage.
items.action: Review pricing and approval logic; prioritize open documents with zero prices.

items.title: Items with negative inventory
items.why: Negative inventory weakens replenishment, delivery commitments, and coordination across warehouse, purchasing, and sales.
items.action: Analyze inventory causes, correct posting sequence, and monitor critical items.

items.title: Customers missing payment terms
items.why: Missing payment terms create follow-ups, inconsistent due dates, and extra collection effort.
items.action: Complete payment terms and embed validation in customer creation.

items.title: Customer ledger overdue over 30 days
items.why: Overdue receivables tie up liquidity and create recurring collection and clarification work.
items.action: Segment overdue entries, assign ownership, and define escalation rules.

items.title: Purchase lines with cost 0
items.why: Zero-cost purchase lines distort acquisition cost, margin, and follow-up costing.
items.action: Introduce price validation before approval and correct affected open documents.

catalog.title: Estimated Loss covers more than isolated master-data issues.

disclaimer.title: Important notice:
disclaimer.text: Estimated Loss is a modeled orientation and decision-support value based on detected data conditions and documented assumptions. It is not a guarantee of costs already incurred, avoidable damage, or savings that will actually be achieved. Customers should validate assumptions such as hourly rate, frequency, and handling time against their own processes.

final.title: Make visible which data issues should be resolved first.
final.lead: Start with the free scan. Assessment unlocks the already generated complete analysis for seven days.
